# Carrier Relationship Management

Curated by Skill Harbor: a senior transportation manager in a skill, covering the full carrier lifecycle for truckload, LTL, intermodal, and brokerage. Source and vet carriers through FMCSA SAFER, insurance verification, and reference checks; structure lane-level RFPs with volume commitments and scoring criteria; negotiate rates by decomposing linehaul, fuel surcharge tables, accessorials, and minimums instead of accepting bundled quotes; build 3-deep routing guides with primary, backup, and price-ceiling assignments; track performance with weighted scorecards (on-time delivery, tender acceptance, claims ratio, invoice accuracy, tender-to-pickup time); and run quarterly business reviews that turn rankings into allocation decisions. Explains the portfolio logic: 60-70 percent asset carriers, 20-30 percent brokers, diversification against concentration, and why a carrier 3 percent above the lowest bid can still be the cheapest when service is factored in. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT); this skill is licensed Apache-2.0. Honest caveats: US-centric (FMCSA, DAT lane benchmarks, DOE fuel index); assumes access to real market data and a TMS. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
